headline: Acquiring 10% of a US tungsten APT processing JV, securing an 8-year offtake of 4,000 tonnes concentrate and US listing planned for next year
reasoning: EQ Resources is entering a joint venture with Almed Group and Blue Moon to restart the Spring APT (ammonium paratungstate) plant in Nevada, funded by $75M from the US Department of War. EQ contributes expertise and feedstock in exchange for a 10% JV interest and an 8-year offtake agreement covering 4,000 tonnes of tungsten in concentrate (500–1,000 tonnes per year, representing up to 25% of plant capacity). China controls 83–85% of global APT and imposed export restrictions in February 2025, creating a supply-chain bifurcation that the company sees as a major tailwind. From January 2027 the US will ban tungsten imports from countries of concern for defence applications, making non-Chinese supply strategically critical. The deal moves EQ from a concentrate producer toward vertical integration with direct access to US end-users. The company is also considering a US listing in the coming year.
quote: So the spring so ammonium para tungsten also known as APT. So the spring APT plant got was started by GE and Utah mining back in the late 70s and 80s around really to to provide tungsten to the to the West. It did go into adventure or it's closed in to care and maintenance in the early 80s largely due to significant price reductions due to significant flows from from China. China controls about 83 to 85% of global APT and they put a restriction on exports in February 2025. And that's what we're starting to see that bifurcation unfold of the tungsten supply chain. From 1 January 2027, there is a ban from the US for any tungsten of from countries of concern where where it could be used in AUS application. So we just see ourselves as a very key part of that process.

headline: Record revenue months in July and August, $22.5M operating cash flow in June, Mount Carbine ramping and Andrew Forrest holds ~17%
reasoning: The company generated $22.5M in operating cash flows in June and achieved record revenue months in both July and August, supported by record production at the Barry mine in Spain in August. The Mount Carbine operation in far North Queensland continues to ramp up as it accesses the in-situ ore body. EQ has also acquired approximately 1,800 sq km of ground adjacent to Mount Carbine and is drilling at the site before moving rigs to Wolfram Camp, an all-tungsten project secured a few years ago. Andrew Forrest acquired close to 17% of EQ Resources from Oaktree at the end of July, which the company views as a strong endorsement from a prominent Australian mining figure.

We've had record revenue months in July and August with a record production of Barry Coppola in Spain in August as well. And the Mont Carbon operation continues to ramp up as we access the in situ body.

headline: China's 83–85% control of global APT supply and February 2025 export restrictions are triggering Western supply-chain bifurcation; US ban on tungsten from countries of concern takes effect January 2027
reasoning: China dominates global ammonium paratungstate production with an 83–85% market share and in February 2025 imposed export restrictions on APT. The US is responding by banning tungsten sourced from countries of concern for defence and strategic applications from 1 January 2027. APT is the cornerstone of all tungsten products used in MRI scanners, military hardware, aircraft, computer chips and more. This structural shift is creating a bifurcated tungsten supply chain, driving urgent demand for non-Chinese processing capacity in the West.
